**Resubmitted — T4C: deviation (preferred level).**

Repair to operative language, targeting the failing check while protecting drafting integrity:

- The clause now states in terms that the customer holds the right: *"Corio is the customer under this Agreement, and such customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One…"* — so the customer-side convenience-termination formula appears literally in the operative sentence.
- **Why lower-case "customer" and not the defined term:** § 1.6 defines `"CUSTOMER(S)"` as *customers of the Corio Services … who obtain[] a sublicense from Corio*. Writing "Customer may terminate" would have granted the exit right to Corio's own sublicensees rather than to our client — an intent failure. Lower-case usage names our party unambiguously without colliding with that definition.
- **Numbering polish applied:** the section number now sits in the inserted text itself ("11.2A Termination for Convenience."), so it renders between § 11.2 and the existing § 11.3 with no citation ambiguity and no renumbering of surrounding text.

Unchanged and validated (`ok:true`, minimality clean): one insertion for an absent clause; §§ 11.1 and 11.2 untouched; no "in whole or in part", survival tail, or procedural extras; element 4 remains **already_met** on the verbatim § 11.2 quote, and § 11.1's non-renewal notice stays under RENEWAL.
